x: Third, not far behind would have been Carl Lawton but he still had a lap to go. However, this position went to Stuart Bennett with the rest of the field strung out over a lap.

Bob Carter was 3rd ahead of last year's winner Bob Whitehead. 5th and 6th positions were filled by the youngsters of the Club Jonathon Dunsford and Stuart Bennett who were told to race between themselves and not against the others.

These two lads have got a promising future if they can retain their ambition and allow it to come steadily. In the Youth's 3 miles we again had two starters, Stuart Bennett and Malcolm Dodds. They produced good efforts for 6th and 7th positions.

The afternoon started with a win for Carl Lawton in the 3 kilos, followed up by Len Duquemin winning the 10 kilos. 1,3 and 4 was the result for Belgrave in the under 18 2 kilo event won convincingly by Martin Bennett with Jonathon Dunsford 3rd and Stuart Bennett next home.
Both Stuart Bennett and Nigel Greaves walked steady races to finish in the top half. In the Senior Boys, Martin Bennett put in a creditable time for 5th position.

A ferocious start by Shaun Maxwell in the Junior/Youth 3km event took him clear of the field and although he faded towards the end he hung on to win in 14:33. Stuart Bennett placed 7th in 15:10. In Rotterdam on the same day, Richard Tanner finished 3rd in a 3km event in 13:54.

In the Middlesex County Championships on 15th May Belgrave Juniors made their mark by filling the first three places in the junior 3km walk. Jonathon Dunsford won in 14:55 with Stuart Bennett only 5 seconds behind in 15:00 and Steve Sharp third in 15:10.
All police cadets they were:- George Nibre, Martin Lewin, Richard Tanner, Tim Thorogood, Terry Moore and Stuart Bennett. Q: In what other aspects of athletics have you been involved?
Nigel Morris, John Dunsford and Stuart Bennett are now expressing their wishes to form a greater part in the team, hence the extra training (and the national trophy).

Down from Birmingham University for the weekend, Simon Williamson showed that he was in good shape, beating Peter Gardner. Stuart Bennett and Jonathon Dunsford, on loan from the walking section, gave the Bels a full turn-out and ran well into the bargain.

Sixth was Jonathon Dunsford, 25:47, 11th Nigel Morris, 26:24, and 14th Stuart Bennett, 27:06. Stuart had placed 6th with 46:50 in a LPR 9 kilometre yacht handicap at Blackheath Park three days earlier.
In the 10,000m Junior Nigel Morris 20th in 56:06 and Stu Bennett 11th in 57:38 were obviously not at their best but worked hard against the odds.
